If you’ve ordered a Taco Bell quesadilla you know how hit or miss they can be, which is especially disappointing when you’re spending that much 😵‍💫 Today I’m showing you how I make their quesadillas at home, start to finish!  This is a big one, so I’ve left all the recipes below, be sure to save this so you can come back and reference! ☺️❤️ 1️⃣ Taco Bell's Creamy Jalapeno Sauce Dupe:  🧾 Ingredients 🧾 One 12-ounce jar pickled jalapeño slices (only 7 Tablespoons of puree needed) 1 teaspoon paprika 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder 1 teaspoon chili powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper 1/2 cup mayonnaise (I am using Dukes, of course) 1/2 cup sour cream 👨‍🍳 Instructions 👨‍🍳 1) Add the entire jar of pickled jalapeño slices, including the liquid, to a blender. Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. The mixture should look like a thin, pale green puree with no visible chunks. 2) In a mixing bowl, combine the mayonnaise, sour cream, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, cayenne pepper, and salt. Stir until the mixture is completely smooth and evenly seasoned. 3) Add seven tablespoons of the blended jalapeño puree to the bowl and mix until fully incorporated. Start with seven tablespoons, then taste and add more puree if desired. Adding too much can make the sauce overly vinegary or too spicy, so increase gradually. 4) Transfer the sauce to an airtight container and refrigerate for at least one hour before using. This resting time allows the flavors to fully develop. The sauce will keep in the refrigerator for up to fourteen days. 2️⃣ Taco Bell Grilled Chicken Dupe 🧾 Ingredients 🧾 1/2 cup water 2 teaspoons kosher salt 1/2 teaspoon MSG 2 teaspoons cornstarch 1 teaspoon chili powder 1 teaspoon paprika 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder 1 teaspoon onion powder 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper 1/2 teaspoon granulated sugar 2 large chicken breasts (about 1 pound total) 1 tablespoon neutral-flavored oil 👨‍🍳 Instructions 👨‍🍳 1) Place one chicken breast flat on a cutting board. Holding it steady with one hand, carefully slice horizontally through the center of the breast to create two thinner, evenly sized chicken fillets. Repeat with the second chicken breast and set the chicken aside while you prepare the marinade. 2) In a medium mixing bowl, combine the water, kosher salt, MSG, cornstarch, chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper and sugar. Whisk until thoroughly combined and the cornstarch has dissolved. 3) Add the chicken to the marinade and toss until each piece is evenly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. 4) Heat the oil in a medium sauté pan over medium-high heat. Once the pan and oil are hot, add two pieces of chicken, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. 5) Cook the chicken for approximately 3–4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through. Check the thickest part of each piece with an instant-read thermometer to ensure the chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 165°F. 6) Transfer the cooked chicken to a plate and repeat with the remaining pieces. Allow the chicken to rest for 5–10 minutes before slicing to help retain its juices. 7) Chop the chicken into your desired size and serve warm in tacos, burritos, quesadillas or bowls. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. #TacoBell #CreamyJalapenoSauce #FastFoodDupe #DishwithDrew #Copycatrecipe
